extracted.intended_audience: newspaper editors, news-service executives, journalists, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and organizational practices governing the receipt, protection, non‑disclosure, and use of news dispatches (in particular Associated Press dispatches) by newspapers and competing news services. Covers prohibitions on disclosure, procedures to safeguard copy, remuneration for tips, and remedial/investigatory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-disclosure of Associated Press matter prior to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: "under no circumstances must they disclose or permit to be disclosed any matter received by said newspaper by or through The Associated Press to any person whatsoever, prior to the time that such news is printed and sold in the New York American, when, of course, it becomes public property." (Bradford Merrill)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers must forbid employees from revealing AP copy or allowing access to outsiders until after publication; the text ties non-disclosure to the point when the paper is printed and sold (becomes public).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Associated Press by-laws and secrecy obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements that furnishing news to the International News Service "was a violation both of the by-laws of the Associated Press and of the orders of the Cleveland News" and references to the "secret and confidential character of the news transmitted to them by complainant." (affidavits and Carvalho)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members and employees of AP member papers are required to observe AP by-laws and to treat transmitted news as secret/confidential until permitted for public use; violations are framed as both by-law and employer-order breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on furnishing news to competitors for consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits describing arrangements whereby deponents "for a consideration paid to the deponent by the said International News Service, he has delivered to the representatives of the International News Service ... information in respect to important items of news" and receiving remuneration (e.g., "five dollars weekly"). (B. E. Gushing, T. J. Thomas)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsroom employees must not enter into paid arrangements to provide incoming AP material or 'tips' to competing services; the page gives examples of checks/vouchers paid by INS and specific weekly amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: No secret telephonic communications of Associated Press news to competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Deponents describe secret telephone calls made from remote parts of the office or private booths to the International News Service to transmit Associated Press news (e.g., "he would leave his desk and go to a private telephone booth or some remote part of the Cleveland News office in order to get secret telephonic communication"). (B. E. Gushing)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural guidance (implicit) is to prohibit covert phone calls or use of remote/secret lines to pass along AP dispatches to competitors; examples include use of booths and avoiding regular switchboard stations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent unauthorized copying/extraction from receiving machines and bulletins
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit recounting that "one of the employees of the International News Service ... make copies of bulletins furnished by The Associated Press to the New York American over the said Morkrum receiving machine" and that an individual "examined the sheets containing the news received ... and made copies or extracts therefrom upon a pad which he has taken away with him." (James Finnerty)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical safeguards are required to prevent outsiders or competing-service staff from reading, copying, or extracting from receiving machines, bulletins, or printed sheets; the example cites copying directly from the Morkrum receiving machine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent physical access of competing-service personnel to editorial/news departments during working hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction to an INS representative: "we cannot permit anyone from the International News Service to be in our editorial or news department at night where he might, even by chance, see Associated Press copy ... During working hours ... I would rather that you would not even enter the news department of the American." (Bradford Merrill)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations should restrict physical presence of outside-service employees in editorial areas while copy is being handled; policy may include barring access during working hours to avoid accidental exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using proofs or early-printed material containing Associated Press copy (even if obtained accidentally)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement that INS should "under no circumstances permit any of the employees of the defendant ... to use any of the telegraphic news proof of the New York American under any circumstances, even if such news, or the proofs thereof, should fall into their hands by accident, for the reason that such proof of telegraphic matter might contain news matter supplied to us by the Associated Press." (Bradford Merrill)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even inadvertent or accidental possession of proofs/early editions that include AP dispatches does not authorize their use; organizations must treat accidental access as non-permissive and refrain from using such material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managers must promulgate and enforce rules to safeguard secrecy and limit access
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertions that publishers "have given orders and adopted and promulgated rules for the government of the employes ... that no employe of the New York American should disclose any news ... or permit any person to have access to the news ... who was not an employe of the New York American, entitled to have access thereto." (Bradford Merrill; S. S. Carvalho)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial leadership must create, communicate, and enforce written or stated rules (physical, procedural, and supervisory) to protect the secrecy of transmitted news and to control which staff may access such copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate allegations of improper acquisition/use of competitor copy and promptly remediate
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate statement: "I have caused to be instituted an investigation of the statements and charges ... If it is found ... that the matters and things charged and described above were, in fact, done ... an end will promptly be put to such practices, and such measures taken to guard against a repetition thereof as may be necessary for that purpose." (S. S. Carvalho)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When improper practices are alleged or suspected (e.g., secret arrangements, payments, or copying), the organization must investigate and take prompt remedial measures to stop the conduct and prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not appropriate Associated Press dispatches (verbatim or paraphrased) for use in competitive service reports intended to enable near-simultaneous publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Witness Hall states he was "expressly instructed by the International News Service to use such Associated Press matter in making up such news reports ... in order that the newspapers purchasing the reports of the International News Service might be able to receive and publish ... the news thus obtained from The Associated Press as nearly as possible simultaneously with the newspapers published by members of The Associated Press," and he "transmitted the said news either in the same text ... or in a paraphrase of his own." (William E. Hall)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News services should not rely on or appropriate another service's dispatches—either verbatim or paraphrased—to supply competing clients in a way that defeats the originating service's exclusivity; the passage documents the practice and its role in the dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inducing members of a news service to violate their membership rules or confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit assertion that defendant "has not induced or attempted to induce any member of the complainant to violate the By-laws of complainant or any agreement created thereby, by which their membership in complainant is controlled, or to disregard the secret and confidential character of the news transmitted to them by complainant." (S. S. Carvalho)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations must refrain from soliciting or encouraging employees or member newspapers of another service to breach their by-laws, confidentiality obligations, or internal orders (explicit prohibition against inducement).
